marks.gloss_en: the baraita: the hide is not susceptible to food impurity
the baraita: 'its carcass' (Lev 11:39) -- and not the hide: the hide does not impart carcass impurity
Rabba bar Rav Chana: [the second baraita] was needed only where one made them into a pot-pudding
the re-scoped question: is a cooked donkey hide susceptible to food impurity?
והתניא: a tree that sheds its fruit -- one paints it red and loads it with stones. בשלמא the stones weaken it; but the red paint, why? -- it has no healing, yet the baraita permits it
the baraita: a tree that sheds its fruit -- one paints it with red paint
the mishna (cited by its lemma): and one does not bury it [the placenta at a crossroads]
מאי טעמא? -- Rav Ika: [because] the males are a minority (completed at 77b.13)
the mishna (cited by its lemma): [the placenta of] an animal bearing its first offspring that miscarried [may be cast to the dogs]
סמוך מיעוטא דנדמה -- the minority of nidmeh is one of the two parts joined
למחצה דנקבות -- the half of females is the other part joined
Rav Ika: and all who give birth bear half males and half females
מאי טעמא? רובא בר מיקדש הוא -- the reason for burial: the majority [of the offspring] is fit to be consecrated
the mishna (cited by its lemma): and with sacrificial animals [the placenta] must be buried
והיינו דאמר רבי ירמיה: לחומרא אמרה ר' אלעזר -- in version 2 R' Elazar's statement is a stringency, as R' Yirmeya said
R' Yochanan (version 2): we have [the mishna's ruling] only for a placenta without a fetus
תניא כוותיה דרבי אלעזר -- not attached: the baraita imposes the stringency of two births
תניא כוותיה דרבי אלעזר -- attached: the baraita is not concerned for another fetus
the baraita: a woman who miscarries a form of domestic animal, wild animal or bird, with a placenta: when it is attached to them, one is not concerned for another fetus

איני? והא אמר רבי ירמיה: לחומרא אמרה רבי אלעזר -- is that so? R' Yirmeya said R' Elazar's statement was a stringency, yet in this version he is the lenient one (kind svara under protest: no objection kind for an amoraic-memra contradiction)
R' Yirmeya: R' Elazar said it as a stringency
R' Elazar (version 1): the mishna taught it only where there is no fetus with it; but where there is a fetus with it, one is not concerned for another fetus
R' Elazar (version 2): the mishna taught it only where [the placenta] is not attached to the fetus -- there one is concerned for another fetus
the baraita's reason: for I say, perhaps the fetus of the placenta dissolved, perhaps the placenta of the fetus dissolved
